Geographic focus:

Synopsis:
Italy recorded its hottest summer since 1950, with August 2026 averaging 25.6°C — surpassing prior records set in 2024 and 2017. Both July and August ranked as warmest on record. Drought and wildfires are aggravating agricultural stress, particularly in northwestern lowlands and along the Apennines. The article situates Italy within a broader pan-European pattern of accelerating heat extremes, noting Britain also logged its hottest summer on record. CNR-IBE signals 2026 is on track to become Italy's hottest year since modern records began.
